_about: Penn State F-1 provisions — what exists, what it requires, and what breaks if you get it wrong. Built by `python -m backend.data.visa_scraper` from global.psu.edu. NOT immigration advice: ACE names the options and the question to ask; only a DSO at Penn State Global can tell a student which applies to them. LLM extraction is not bit-for-bit reproducible — diff before committing.

records.title: Full-Time Enrollment
records.what_it_is: Both F-1 and J-1 students must maintain full-time academic status.
records.when_it_applies: For F-1 or J-1 students enrolled at Penn State.
conditions: Undergraduate and Law students must enroll for a minimum of 12 credits/semester.
Graduate students must enroll in a minimum of 9 credits/semester.
F-1 and J-1 students may count no more than 3 hybrid-remote/online credits toward their minimum requirement.
numbers: 12 credits minimum for undergraduate and Law students
9 credits minimum for graduate students
3 hybrid-remote/online credits maximum
records.risk_if_wrong: Dropping below full-time enrollment without authorization is a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What are the consequences of dropping below full-time enrollment?

records.title: Part-Time Enrollment/Reduced Course Load
records.what_it_is: Part-time enrollment/exceptions to full-time study must be cleared with an International Student Adviser in advance.
records.when_it_applies: When a student needs to enroll part-time instead of full-time.
records.risk_if_wrong: Part-time enrollment without authorization is a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Meet with your International Student Adviser.
records.ask_adviser: What are the approved reasons for a reduced course load?

records.title: Hybrid, Web-Based, or Online Courses
records.what_it_is: F-1 and J-1 students may count only 3 credits that are taught hybrid-remote/online toward full-time enrollment each semester.
records.when_it_applies: When enrolling in hybrid-remote/online courses.
numbers: 3 hybrid-remote/online credits maximum
records.risk_if_wrong: Counting more than 3 hybrid-remote/online credits toward full-time enrollment is a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Review the course schedule for hybrid-remote/online options.
records.ask_adviser: How do hybrid-remote/online courses affect my full-time status?

records.title: World Campus Enrollment
records.what_it_is: F-1 and J-1 students cannot do a change of campus to World Campus and remain in the United States.
records.when_it_applies: When considering enrollment in World Campus while in the U.S.
records.risk_if_wrong: Full-time enrollment in World Campus within the U.S. is a violation of F-1 and J-1 status.
records.how_to_start: Consult with your International Student Adviser before making changes.
records.ask_adviser: Can I take World Campus courses while in the U.S.?

records.title: Summer Enrollment Requirements
records.what_it_is: Undergraduate and graduate students beginning their degree during the summer must meet specific credit requirements.
records.when_it_applies: For students starting their degree in the summer semester.
conditions: Undergraduate students must be registered for 12 credits.
Graduate students must be registered for 9 credits.
F-1 and J-1 students may count no more than 3 hybrid-remote/online credits toward their minimum requirement.
numbers: 12 credits minimum for undergraduate students
9 credits minimum for graduate students
3 hybrid-remote/online credits maximum
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to meet these requirements can jeopardize immigration status.
records.how_to_start: Register for summer courses as per the requirements.
records.ask_adviser: What are the specific requirements for summer enrollment?

records.title: F-1 Regulations
records.what_it_is: As an F-1 international student, you are required to enroll in a full-time course load or have approval for a reduced course load.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to all F-1 international students.
conditions: Enroll in a full-time course load or have approval for a reduced course load.
Enroll in the correct number of in-person credits.
Enroll in courses while you have an active SEVIS record.
records.risk_if_wrong: A violation will result in a student’s SEVIS record being terminated. When this occurs, there is no grace period, and the student is required to leave the U.S. immediately.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What are the specific requirements for maintaining my full-time enrollment status?

records.title: Academic Difficulty
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to request a reduced course load due to initial academic difficulties.
records.when_it_applies: For students facing initial academic difficulty due to language, reading requirements, unfamiliarity with American teaching methods, or improper course level placement.
conditions: This reason can be used only one time per degree program.
Initial academic difficulty due to problems with English language: 1st semester only.
Initial academic difficulty due to the reading requirements: 1st year only.
Initial academic difficulty due to student being unfamiliar with American teaching methods: 1st year only.
Improper course level placement.
numbers: Undergraduate students: 6 credits (with a minimum of 3 in-person and no more than 3 online/hybrid/remote credits)
Graduate students: 5 credits (with a minimum of 3 in-person and no more than 3 online/hybrid/remote credits)
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to meet enrollment requirements violates your immigration status, which ISSA must report and may jeopardize your active status.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: I used academic-difficulty RCL in my first semester — can I use a different reason now?

records.title: Last Semester of Enrollment
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to request a reduced course load during their final semester of enrollment.
records.when_it_applies: For students completing their degree program requirements, including thesis or paper defense.
conditions: For students in non-thesis programs: The last semester is your final semester of enrollment.
For graduate students and others in programs that require a thesis or paper: Your last semester is the final semester of enrollment and thesis or paper defense.
numbers: Undergraduate students and graduate students without a thesis requirement: 3 in-person credits required for your program (with a minimum of 3 in-person and no more than 3 online/hybrid/remote credits)
Graduate students with a thesis requirement: 1 in-person credit required for your program.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to meet enrollment requirements violates your immigration status, which ISSA must report and may jeopardize your active status.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: Does my thesis defence term count as my final semester for the I-20 end date?

records.title: Medical or Psychological Reasons
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to request a reduced course load for medical or psychological reasons.
records.when_it_applies: For students receiving treatment at University Health Services or Counseling and Psychological Services, or those who submit documentation from a licensed physician or psychiatrist.
conditions: Requests are reviewed by University Health Services or Counseling and Psychological Services.
Students must either receive treatment at UHS or CAPS, or submit documentation from a licensed physician (to UHS) or psychiatrist (to CAPS) for review.
Approval of a reduced course load for these reasons is limited to a maximum of 12 months total.
numbers: These RCL requests are granted per semester.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to meet enrollment requirements violates your immigration status, which ISSA must report and may jeopardize your active status.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What documentation do I need to submit for a medical or psychological RCL?

records.title: F-1 On-Campus Employment Policies
records.what_it_is: As an F-1 student, you are allowed to work on-campus for Penn State.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to F-1 students who are enrolled at Penn State.
conditions: You may work up to 20 hours per week while school is in session.
Continuing students may work full time (over 20 hours per week) in the summer.
numbers: 20 hours per week while school is in session
over 20 hours per week in the summer for continuing students
records.risk_if_wrong: Working more than the allowed hours without authorization is a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Obtain an employment letter from the hiring department.
records.ask_adviser: What steps do I need to take to start working on-campus?
side_effects: Potential impact on academic performance due to work hours
Possible effects on financial aid eligibility

records.title: F-1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) - Eligibility Requirements
records.what_it_is: CPT allows F-1 students to engage in internships or employment that is integral to their academic program.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who need practical training as part of their degree requirements.
conditions: Must have lawful, full-time enrollment for one academic year.
CPT must occur before the program end date on your I-20.
The training/internship must be required by the academic program.
The opportunity must be closely related to the major of study.
The training must happen before completing all coursework.
records.risk_if_wrong: Unauthorized CPT can lead to a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: Does my unpaid internship require CPT authorization?

records.title: F-1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) - Part-time vs. Full-time
records.what_it_is: CPT can be authorized for part-time or full-time work.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who are engaging in CPT.
numbers: Part-time: 20 hours or fewer per week.
Full-time: more than 20 hours per week.

records.title: F-1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) - Effect of CPT on Optional Practical Training (OPT)
records.what_it_is: Accumulating full-time CPT can affect eligibility for OPT.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who have engaged in full-time CPT.
numbers: If you accumulate 365 days or more of full-time CPT, you will not be eligible for OPT.

records.title: F-1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) - Application and Authorization Process
records.what_it_is: This outlines the steps to apply for CPT authorization.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who have secured an internship or employment.
records.risk_if_wrong: Continuing to work beyond the authorized date on your I-20 without an extension can lead to a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Fill out the Curricular Practical Training (CPT) form in iStart.
records.ask_adviser: What details must be included in the employer letter for CPT?

records.title: F-1 Curricular Practical Training (CPT) - Updating Your Address While on CPT
records.what_it_is: Students must keep their current address updated in SEVIS while on CPT.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who are currently engaged in CPT.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failure to update your address can lead to compliance issues with the Department of Homeland Security.
records.how_to_start: Complete the U.S. Local Address Update form in iStart.

records.title: Post-Completion OPT Eligibility
records.what_it_is: Post-Completion Optional Practical Training (OPT) allows F-1 students to gain up to 12 months of practical experience in their field of study after completing their degree.
records.when_it_applies: When a student is nearing completion of their degree and meets the eligibility requirements for Post-Completion OPT.
conditions: Have not been approved for a total of 365 days of full-time CPT.
Were enrolled full-time for at least one academic year (two semesters).
Have maintained active F-1 status.
Will complete your degree in the near future.
numbers: up to 12 months of practical experience
365 days maximum of full-time CPT
two semesters minimum enrollment
records.risk_if_wrong: If a student applies for OPT without meeting the eligibility requirements, they may violate their F-1 status.
records.how_to_start: Request an OPT I-20 in iStart.
records.ask_adviser: Can I apply for OPT if I have used full-time CPT previously?
side_effects: Potential impact on tuition and financial aid eligibility.
Delay in graduation timing if application is not submitted correctly.

records.title: Applying for OPT: A Two-Step Process
records.what_it_is: The process for applying for Post-Completion OPT involves requesting an OPT I-20 and submitting the application to USCIS.
records.when_it_applies: When a student is ready to apply for Post-Completion OPT after meeting eligibility requirements.
numbers: Apply for OPT as early as 90 days before your program end date.
Submit your OPT application within 30 days of the date of OPT I-20 issuance or by the 60th day from the program end date, whichever comes first.
The OPT application window closes on the 60th day from the program end date.
records.risk_if_wrong: Submitting the application late may result in the inability to work on OPT.
records.how_to_start: Submit form I-765, the signed I-20 with the OPT recommendation, and other required documents to USCIS online.
records.ask_adviser: What is the best time to submit my OPT application?
side_effects: Inability to work on campus past the I-20 program end date unless on OPT.
Need to maintain enrollment if summer is the final term.

records.title: Pre-Completion OPT
records.what_it_is: Pre-completion OPT allows students to work either full-time or part-time while enrolled in their academic program, or during summer vacation, as long as they will enroll for the upcoming fall semester.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who have been enrolled continuously for one academic year and are in active F-1 status.
conditions: Have been enrolled continuously for one academic year (fall and spring semester) by the time the Pre-completion OPT employment starts.
Be in active F-1 status.
Your Pre-completion OPT employment must be closely related to your major of study.
numbers: Eligible for 12 months of OPT for each higher-level degree.
Full-time Pre-completion OPT is deducted at a one-to-one ratio from the 12-month total.
Part-time Pre-completion OPT is deducted at half the rate from the 12-month total.
You may apply for Pre-completion OPT 90 days prior to the end of the one academic year.
Submit form I-765 within 30 days of the date of OPT I-20 issuance.
records.risk_if_wrong: If you apply and are approved for Pre-completion OPT for a total of 12 months, you will no longer be eligible for Post-completion OPT.
records.how_to_start: Request the I-20 by completing the OPT form in iStart.
records.ask_adviser: What documents do I need to submit with my OPT application?
side_effects: Any unused days of OPT cannot be recovered once approved.
It takes approximately 90 days to receive the EAD card.

records.title: Cap-Gap Extension
records.what_it_is: The Cap-Gap extension allows students on Post-Completion or STEM OPT to continue working between the end of their OPT authorized period and the beginning of the H-1B period if their employer filed the H-1B petition in a timely manner.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to students who are on Post-Completion or STEM OPT and have a timely filed H-1B petition.
conditions: The H-1B petition must be filed in a timely manner.
If not approved for OPT or in the 60-day grace period after OPT has ended, the student is eligible for an extension of F-1 status but may not work during the Cap-Gap period.
numbers: 60-day grace period if the H-1B petition is rejected, denied, or revoked.
records.risk_if_wrong: If the H-1B petition is not approved, the Cap-Gap extension will terminate, and the student will enter a 60-day grace period.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account and complete the Cap Gap form.
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if my H-1B petition is denied?
side_effects: May affect work authorization and status if the H-1B petition is not approved.

records.title: Volunteering
records.what_it_is: Volunteering is working for an individual or an organization in an unpaid position for humanitarian, public service, or religious reasons with no expectation of remuneration or compensation.
records.when_it_applies: When an international student wishes to volunteer without compensation.
conditions: Volunteering must be for humanitarian, public service, or religious reasons.
Volunteering cannot be for for-profit private sector employers.
Activities that are normally considered paid employment cannot be volunteered.
records.risk_if_wrong: Engaging in activities that are considered employment without proper authorization can lead to a violation of status.
records.how_to_start: Review how the U.S. Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) defines volunteering.
records.ask_adviser: If I volunteer in a position that is normally paid, will it affect my status?

records.title: Unpaid Internship
records.what_it_is: For International students in F-1 status, internships (unpaid or paid) require authorization from ISSA.
records.when_it_applies: When an international student wants to participate in an unpaid internship.
conditions: An unpaid internship may fall under Curricular Practical Training (CPT).
Students must have been lawfully enrolled full-time for one academic year to be eligible for CPT.
Students in English language programs are ineligible for practical training.
numbers: Must be lawfully enrolled full-time for one academic year.
records.risk_if_wrong: Participating in an unpaid internship without authorization can lead to a violation of status.
records.how_to_start: Review information on how to request Curricular Practical Training (CPT).
records.ask_adviser: What steps do I need to take to get authorization for an unpaid internship?

records.title: F-1 On-Campus Employment
records.what_it_is: F-1 international students are allowed to work on campus under certain eligibility requirements.
records.when_it_applies: When F-1 international students meet the eligibility requirements for on-campus employment.
conditions: Must maintain valid F-1 status
Must be enrolled full-time during the academic year
Employment must not exceed 20 hours per week during the academic year
numbers: 20 hours per week during the academic year
records.risk_if_wrong: Working without authorization or exceeding the allowed hours can lead to a violation of F-1 status.
records.how_to_start: Contact your International Student Adviser for guidance on employment opportunities.
records.ask_adviser: What are the specific eligibility requirements for on-campus employment?
side_effects: Potential impact on academic performance
Possible effects on financial aid eligibility

records.title: F-1 Severe Economic Hardship - Authorized Off-Campus Employment
records.what_it_is: This provision allows F-1 students to work off-campus due to severe economic hardship.
records.when_it_applies: When unforeseen circumstances beyond the student's control cause financial problems.
conditions: Maintain F-1 status for a full academic year
Be in good academic standing and enrolled full-time (unless approved for a Reduced Course Load)
Make a good faith effort to obtain on-campus employment before applying
Discuss with an International Student Adviser
numbers: Limited to 20 hours of work per week while school is in session
Full time only during vacation periods and summers
records.risk_if_wrong: Unauthorized off-campus employment can lead to a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Access the iStart account to begin the application process.
records.ask_adviser: What documentation do I need to provide for severe economic hardship?
side_effects: Potential impact on tuition and financial aid
May affect graduation timing

records.title: Violation of Penn State's Code of Conduct and Your Immigration Status
records.what_it_is: Activities that violate Penn State's code of conduct standards may affect your immigration status in the U.S.
records.when_it_applies: If a violation of Penn State's code of conduct results in your inability to enroll.
records.risk_if_wrong: If your SEVIS record is terminated for this reason, you will not have a grace period and will be required to leave the U.S. immediately.
records.how_to_start: Know and abide by the laws of the U.S.
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if I am accused of violating the code of conduct?
side_effects: Loss of enrollment
Immediate departure from the U.S.

records.title: Correcting a Terminated F-1 Record
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to apply for a new F-1 record to resume their studies in the U.S. after a withdrawal, military service, suspension, or leave of absence.
records.when_it_applies: When a student wishes to return to Penn State for in-person studies after a withdrawal, military service, suspension, or leave of absence.
conditions: Complete the re-enrollment process with the Registrar’s Office (undergraduates) or through the Fox Graduate School (graduate students).
ISSA can process your returning student I-20 only after confirmation of approval to return by the Registrar’s Office or your department.
Request a new I-20 about 3 months before the date of your approved return to the University.
numbers: Request a new I-20 about 3 months before the date of your approved return.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to apply for a new F-1 record can result in a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account and complete the Returning Students form.
records.ask_adviser: What documents do I need to upload with my Returning Students form?
side_effects: Potential delays in resuming studies.
Impact on financial aid and tuition status.

records.title: Leave of Absence
records.what_it_is: A student is allowed to apply for a Leave of Absence for a period of time and return to continue their degree program.
records.when_it_applies: When a student needs to take a break from their studies for personal reasons.
conditions: Apply for a Leave of Absence with the Registrar's Office or, for graduate students, with the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School.
The deadline for applying is the last business day before the first day of classes for the semester that the leave will begin.
numbers: usually up to one year
records.risk_if_wrong: Your I-20/DS-2019 record will be closed down as a result, which ends your active F-1/J-1 SEVIS status.
records.who_authorises: Registrar's Office or J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School
records.how_to_start: Apply for a Leave of Absence with the appropriate office.
records.ask_adviser: What are the implications for my immigration status if I take a Leave of Absence?

records.title: Withdrawal
records.what_it_is: If a student is unable to complete the semester, they may choose to withdraw from the University.
records.when_it_applies: When a student cannot complete the semester and considers withdrawing.
conditions: Refer to the Registrar’s website to see the university process to withdraw or, for graduate students, the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School website.
Discuss your situation with an International Student Adviser to determine the timing of leaving the U.S.
records.risk_if_wrong: Your I-20/DS-2019 record will be closed down as a result of the withdrawal, which ends your active F-1/J-1 SEVIS status.
records.who_authorises: Registrar's Office or J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School
records.how_to_start: Refer to the appropriate website for the withdrawal process.
records.ask_adviser: What are the consequences of withdrawing on my immigration status?

records.title: Travel Signature Validity
records.what_it_is: This provision outlines the validity period of travel signatures for F-1 and J-1 students.
records.when_it_applies: For current F-1/J-1 students planning to travel abroad.
conditions: Only ISSA advisers who are a Designated School Official (DSO) or Alternate Responsible Officer (ARO) can sign a Penn State I-20/DS-2019.
numbers: Travel signature is valid for 12 months or until the end of the program of study, whichever is sooner for current F-1/J-1 students.
Travel signature is valid for 6 months for F-1 students on Post-Completion OPT/STEM OPT or J-1 students on Academic Training.
records.risk_if_wrong: Traveling without a valid travel signature can result in being unable to re-enter the U.S.
records.how_to_start: Complete the Travel Signature form in iStart, under Other Requests, well in advance of travel.
records.ask_adviser: How do I ensure my travel signature is valid before I travel?
side_effects: Potential delays in re-entry to the U.S.
Issues with maintaining student status.

records.title: F-1 I-20 Extension
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to request an extension of their I-20 if they cannot complete their academic program by the program end date listed on their I-20.
records.when_it_applies: When a student will not complete their academic program by the program end date on their I-20.
conditions: Submit your extension request in iStart no later than 45 days before the expiration date of your I-20.
Have maintained and are currently maintaining F-1 immigration status.
Full-time enrollment (unless you have been approved for a Reduced Course Load through ISSA).
The delay is caused by compelling academic or medical reasons, such as changes of major or research topics, unexpected research problems, or documented illnesses.
You are progressing normally toward your educational degree.
numbers: no later than 45 days before the expiration date of your I-20
summer in-person enrollment is required if summer is your final semester
records.risk_if_wrong: You will not be able to request an extension after your I-20 expires, which could lead to a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Submit an extension request in iStart (listed under I-20 or DS-2019 Requests).
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if I have compelling academic reasons for needing an extension?
side_effects: Potential impact on tuition and financial aid
Graduation timing may be delayed

records.title: Grace Period for F-1 and J-1 Students
records.what_it_is: A grace period allows students to take action to continue their lawful stay in the U.S. after completing their studies.
records.when_it_applies: Upon completion of studies for F-1 and J-1 students.
conditions: F-1 students have a 60-day grace period.
J-1 students have a 30-day grace period.
Students must take action within the grace period.
numbers: 60 days for F-1 students
30 days for J-1 students
records.risk_if_wrong: If a student does not take any action, they must depart by the end of the grace period.
records.how_to_start: Complete the Exit form in iStart to inform of your plan to return home.
records.ask_adviser: What actions can I take during my grace period?
side_effects: Potential impact on future visa applications
Ineligibility for certain benefits if not properly managed

records.title: Transferring to a New Institution
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to transfer their SEVIS record to a new institution.
records.when_it_applies: When a student wishes to move from Penn State to another school.
conditions: Must submit the SEVIS Transfer Out form in iStart.
Must upload the admission/acceptance letter from the new school.
No transfer request will be processed without a completed iStart form and an admission letter.
J-1 students must be sure they are eligible for the transfer before making this request.
numbers: Must begin at the new school within 5 months of the last date of attendance or on the next available session start date, whichever is earlier.
Graduating students must request a transfer date within their 60-day grace period.
records.risk_if_wrong: Transferring without authorization can lead to a status violation, and students may not receive a refund of tuition or may receive all 'W' grades on their transcript.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account and submit the SEVIS Transfer Out form.
records.ask_adviser: What should I consider when choosing my transfer release date?
side_effects: May not receive a refund of tuition money if transferring in the middle of a semester.
May receive all 'W' grades on the transcript for the semester if transferring mid-semester.

records.title: Lost or Stolen Documents
records.what_it_is: This provision outlines the steps to take if your passport or other important documents are lost or stolen.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to international students in F-1 or J-1 status who have lost or had their passport stolen.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to replace lost or stolen documents can jeopardize your legal status in the U.S.
records.how_to_start: Request a police report at the local police station.
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if my passport is lost or stolen?
side_effects: Potential delays in travel, issues with on-campus work, and complications with visa status.

records.title: Change of Major
records.what_it_is: F-1 students can request a new document to change their major by completing the Change of Major form in iStart.
records.when_it_applies: This applies to F-1 students who need to update their major.
conditions: This form is only for F-1 students.
Typically, J-1 students cannot change their major as it is considered a change in program objective.
records.risk_if_wrong: Your I-20 or DS-2019 must reflect accurate information; failing to do so may lead to status issues.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if I notice a mistake on my I-20 or DS-2019?

records.title: Change of Academic Level
records.what_it_is: This provision allows students to change their academic degree level while at Penn State and receive a new I-20 or DS-2019.
records.when_it_applies: When a student accepts an offer of admission at a new program degree level.
conditions: Must accept an offer of admission at the new program degree level.
Must complete the Change of Level form in iStart and submit new financial documentation.
A new I-20/DS-2019 must be issued no later than the end of the grace period.
Enrollment in the new program must begin at the next available session start date but no more than 5 months from the end of the last program.
numbers: 5 months from the end of the last program for enrollment in the new program.
records.risk_if_wrong: Failing to maintain status while changing academic levels can lead to a status violation.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What steps do I need to take to ensure my I-20 reflects my new academic level?
side_effects: Potential impact on tuition and financial aid.
Graduation timing may be affected.

records.title: Social Security Number
records.what_it_is: The Social Security Number (SSN) is needed when employers report wages to the government. The Social Security Administration (SSA) will issue a Social Security Number (SSN), upon request, to international students for employment purposes only.
records.when_it_applies: When an international student needs to work in the U.S. and requires an SSN for employment purposes.
conditions: An SSN is not necessary for establishing a bank account, renting an apartment, or opening a cell phone account.
If someone insists on providing an SSN for the above instances, they should contact ISSA.
records.risk_if_wrong: Providing an SSN when not required can lead to unnecessary complications and potential misuse of personal information.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What documents do I need to apply for an SSN?

records.title: Health Insurance Requirement
records.what_it_is: It is mandatory for all international students in F-1 and J-1 status and for their accompanying dependents to have health insurance.
records.when_it_applies: All international students in F-1 and J-1 status and their dependents.
conditions: Students must either purchase insurance through the Penn State Insurance Office or apply for a waiver by providing evidence of current health insurance coverage that meets the Penn State insurance standards.
Students have the first week to apply for an insurance waiver if they have insurance meeting all of the waiver standards.
numbers: Graduate Assistants and Graduate Fellows are automatically enrolled in the Penn State insurance plan.
Penn State covers 80% of the insurance premium for the graduate assistant/fellow and 70% of the premium for dependents.
records.risk_if_wrong: Willful violation of this mandate requires termination of the J-1 status.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What are the waiver standards for health insurance?
side_effects: Health insurance charges will be on the student bill in LionPATH for all international students.
Students will be automatically enrolled in the Student Health Insurance Program (SHIP) if they do not apply for a waiver.

records.title: Updating Address and Contact Information
records.what_it_is: Students in F-1 and J-1 status are required to report and update their address and contact information.
records.when_it_applies: While you are a student and after graduation while on OPT or STEM Extension OPT.
conditions: You must report both your home country address and your local U.S. address.
You must update your local U.S. address in iStart within 10 days every time it changes.
If you change your address while working on campus, you must fill out a new W-4 form with your Penn State Employer.
All off-campus employment requires authorization through ISSA.
After graduation, you must report any address change within 10 days of occurrence.
numbers: 10 days for updating local U.S. address
10 days for reporting address change after graduation
records.risk_if_wrong: Failure to report your address can lead to a violation of your immigration status.
records.how_to_start: Access your iStart account.
records.ask_adviser: What should I do if I change my address while on OPT?
side_effects: Potential issues with employment authorization
Impact on immigration status
